subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Debt and Cognitive Load
description: A micro-lesson that makes Debt and Cognitive Load usable.

hook.text: People in debt score 13 IQ points lower on cognitive tests. Not because they're less smart.

buildup.text: Mullainathan and Shafir's scarcity research showed that financial stress occupies working memory, leaving less.

discovery.text: Debt creates a tax on thinking. Every decision is filtered through 'can I afford this?' draining energy from everything.

twist.text: This creates a vicious cycle: debt impairs decision-making, which leads to worse financial choices, which creates more.

climax.text: Reducing debt doesn't just save money. It frees mental capacity for better decisions across every domain of life.

punchline.text: Debt doesn't just cost money. It costs thinking.

quiz.question: How does debt affect cognitive performance?
options: It has no effect on thinking
It occupies working memory, reducing capacity for other decisions
It makes people permanently less intelligent
